_comment: Decided on 2026-08-11 against the real export (2,710 events) and the live
event_article schema. Each entry says what was settled and why, so a later
reader does not reopen a closed question. Anything 'pending' waits on the
named party, not on us. Same shape as config/types/blogs.json.
The routing and image rules below are implemented in
Events-Pipeline/pipeline/build_portal.py and are NOT yet in pipeline/taxonomy/.

banner_image.note: imageurl is the banner. Where it is empty and attachment_files has a file, the attachment becomes the banner - 933 events would otherwise publish with no hero while holding an unused image. Result: 2,667 of 2,710 have a hero, 12 have neither column filled, 31 are named but not on disk.

second_image.note: Only 32 events have BOTH imageurl and attachment_files. For those the attachment becomes an image node at the BOTTOM of the rich text, inside it rather than as a standalone image blok - news's rule, because the standalone blok renders far too large. THE POSITION IS A HOUSE CONVENTION: SharePoint records none. All 2,710 bodies contain zero and none names the file. 'After the first paragraph' was tried and measured - it sat between two paragraphs only 51% of the time and was stranded at the end for 16%, because 194 bodies have a single paragraph.

location.note: location <- Venue, not Country. Every event has a venue and 'where is it' means the room, not the country - the folder already says the country. Cost: Venue is HTML and location is plain text, so 639 links across 504 events flatten. 2,206 venues contain no link and map cleanly. 51 exceed 255 characters; 1 is markup only and strips to nothing.

country.note: Country chooses the region folder and has no visible field. It is not lost - the folder is how the page states its country.

routing.note: Entity folder, else region folder, else global/events. Nothing is ever created; every candidate is checked against the live tree. Region comes from Country, else City. Where no column locates an event, news rule 5 applies - an entity whose located events are >=60% in one region takes its unlocated ones there, because the tree records who OWNS an item, not where it happened. That moved 27 events. An explicit Global is never second-guessed. Result: 2,319 entity, 314 region, 77 global, 0 unrouted.

entity_alias.note: 'Network of Quality, Teaching and Learning' is mapped to 'Networks of Quality, Teaching and Learning' - singular/plural of one unit, both spellings in the same export, and the plural already owns the qtl folder. This maps onto an existing entity; it does not create one.

city_spelling.note: 'Dar es Salam' (missing an 'a', 2 rows) is recorded as a variant in the city lookup rather than corrected in the export - CODING_STANDARDS section 4.

event_types.note: Tags is single-valued, 16 clean values reconciling exactly with Tags.csv, no orphans either way. event_types is a custom event-types-plugin whose vocabulary is NOT knowable from the space - /field_types returns 403 to a personal token, and the one filled value seen anywhere is 'conf-workshop', which reads as Conference AND Workshop merged. So the map is probably many-to-one. Needs the 16 labels mapped to the plugin's slugs.

contact.note: Populated on ALL 2,710 events, 2,046 links across 1,251. event_article has no contact field at all. The single largest gap.

registration.note: register_label = 'Register Now' and register_link = the URL out of the Registration column, written as an EXTERNAL multilink. Filled on 799: 768 have a real <a href>, and 31 more have a bare URL in the text, which is still SharePoint's link. 93 events carry more than one link (up to 7) and the FIRST is taken -- the one the registration sentence leads with; the rest stay in the body. The remaining 132 have Registration as prose ('Registration is Free') with no URL: BOTH fields are left empty, because no link means no button and a label on its own is dead weight. SharePoint escapes colons as :, so hrefs are unescaped before writing or every link would be broken. CLOSED, not pending: the 132 with no URL are left with both fields empty and are not chased further. About 31 are fragments ('reg', blanks); the rest carry prose - 12 email addresses, 13 deadlines, 1 phone number, and a few 'Click here to register' whose <a> did not survive the export, so the destination is gone from the cell entirely. No link means no button. The Registration text itself is dropped for ALL 931 events, since event_article has no registration field; it stays in data/events.json and in the payload, so an update plan can fill it later if the dev ever adds one.

unmapped_columns.note: No field on event_article: EventSubTitle (1,713), ImageCredit (1,538), EventSite (147), OtherCity (107), EventSubsite (74), SocialMedia (1), OnGoingEvent (123 true).

no_source_column.note: event_article has `mode` and `deadline`; the export has neither. The reference page fills both by hand. They stay empty unless AKU supplies them.

archive_not_upcoming.note: ALL 2,710 events are in the past - StartDate runs 2007-10-30 to 2026-04-18 and the latest ended months ago. event_article carries register_link, register_label and show_calendar, and the space has an upcoming_events component. Publishing 'Register Now' on a 2015 workshop is wrong. Needs a decision on whether the registration UI is suppressed for past events.

no_shared_entities.note: AdditionalEntity is present and EMPTY on all 2,710, so events has no cross-entity sharing to migrate - and event_article has no `entities` field to hold it anyway (entity is a plain text field). News's build_crossrefs / share_target machinery does not apply. Worth one question to AKU on whether it was never used or just not exported.

dates.note: start_at and end_at are real `datetime` fields and take StartDate/EndDate with the seconds trimmed ('2015-03-09 14:30'); 124 events have no EndDate. event_date is 'Mar 09, 2015', or 'Mar 09 - Jul 10, 2015' where the event spans days. event_time takes the clock times off StartDate and EndDate as the DAILY session, including for multi-day courses -- 626 of the 670 multi-day events with times have a start earlier in the day than the end, which is what a class slot looks like: #8 is a 16-week course running 14:30-18:30 daily. Filled on 2,464 of 2,710; the 246 blanks are events whose StartDate time is 00:00, so SharePoint has no time to import. deadline = StartDate, formatted like event_date; the export has no deadline column. RULE: whatever SharePoint holds is imported as-is. Nothing is dropped or reshaped on judgement.

mode.note: mode = 'In-Person' on all 2,710. The export has no mode column; event_article's own description reads 'e.g. In-Person, Online, Hybrid'.

switches.note: show_calendar, show_share, show_events and show_events_header are all true on every event. Constants, not from the export, and written explicitly rather than left to the component defaults - only show_calendar defaults true in the schema, and a default can change under us. Note this means all 2,710 archived events render an Add to Calendar button; start_at/end_at exist only to drive it, per the field's own description.

intro_heading.note: Every event body opens with a rich_text blok holding an H1 'About this <Tag>', with the tag word in the brand green (#008F51) as a textStyle mark. Shape copied field for field off events-detail/test; the wording comes from the SharePoint Tags column, which is single-valued and clean. It sits ahead of the converted EventDetail, so every event has two or more rich_text bloks. Four tags are reworded so the heading reads as English, and the rewording is the whole heading, not just the word -- '40 years of AKU' drops 'this': Other and untagged -> 'About this Event'; '40 years of AKU' -> 'About 40 Years of AKU'; 'Grand Rounds' -> 'About this Grand Round'; 'Open day' -> 'About this Open Day'. The green covers the word after the prefix in every case.

location_online.rule: Venue says online and names no physical place -> location = "Online".
location_online.counts: 715 of 2,710 set to Online (473 unambiguous + 242 with extra text). 67 left alone because the word arrives inside "Register online" beside a real room. 1,504 were already clean.
location_online.why_not_all_782: A literal 'contains the word online' rule would replace "Lecture Hall 3 & CIME PBL Rooms, Medical College, AKU" with "Online" on 67 events. Measured before adopting.

location_cta_junk.rule: 423 venues carry CTA/nav blocks and no "online" -- "AKU Auditorium R E G I S T R A T I O N Register for the course Fee...". LEFT EXACTLY AS SHAREPOINT HAS THEM.
location_cta_junk.rejected_alternative: A cut-at-first-CTA-marker rule was written and measured: 231 of 423 shortened, 0 emptied. Not adopted -- the standing rule is to import what SharePoint has. Do not re-derive it; the evidence is in Events-Pipeline/data/venue_review.csv.

location_word_paste.rule: strip_html now drops <style>/<script> CONTENTS and Word conditional comments, not just the tags.
location_word_paste.why: 7 Venue values are Word paste. Event 242 published as "Conference Room, Emergency Medicine Normal 0 false false false EN-US X-NONE /* Style Definitions */ table.MsoNormalTable {mso-style-name:...}". Removing tags alone leaves the CSS text, because <style> holds text rather than markup.

event_date_start_only.rule: event_date is the START date only, never a range.
event_date_start_only.why: An earlier version rendered the 871 multi-day events as "Sep 20 - Sep 22, 2019". The span is not lost: start_at and end_at are real datetime fields carrying both ends exactly.

richtext_document_links.rule: Document links in the body are rewritten to the uploaded Storyblok asset URL at payload-build time.
richtext_document_links.why: attach-richtext-media wrote /events-media/<file> at stage 1, when nothing had been uploaded and no real URL existed. 163 documents across 120 events would otherwise 404 -- mostly the programmes and registration forms those pages exist for.

text_clean_adopted.rule: Events uses pipeline/core/text_clean.py -- clean_text for plain fields, clean_richtext for the body -- rather than its own helpers.
text_clean_adopted.why: CLAUDE.md 9 landed on master naming events directly. Measured: the export holds 79,495 HTML entities and 2,353 were reaching the built payloads (" 1,420,   795, & 80), to publish as literal text mid-sentence. Now 0, verified on all 2,710 and on the 10 live.
text_clean_adopted.markers: {pullquote} and {EmbeddedCode} do not occur in events -- counted, 0 of 2,710. The shared cleaner strips them anyway.
text_clean_adopted.slugs: Unchanged: 0 of 2,710 differ after the switch, so no story moves.
text_clean_adopted.shared_change: text_clean.strip_html now drops <style>/<script> CONTENTS and Word conditional comments, not just the tags. Contributed there rather than kept in events because news has 46 of the same blocks, which is the two-code-paths fault CLAUDE.md 9 exists to prevent.
text_clean_adopted.guard: build_payload warns if looks_encoded() finds anything surviving.

payload_builder_is_declared.rule: storyblok.payload_builder names the type's own builder. The shared uploader never discovers one by filename.
payload_builder_is_declared.why: The merge brought Blogs-Pipeline/pipeline/build_payload.py, whose build() is build(story, routing, authors, photos, palette) and is driven by blogs' own upload.py. Filename discovery would have adopted it for --type blogs and called it with six arguments it has never seen. Blogs is safe today only because it does not use the shared cmd_stories; that is luck, not design.

_comment: What pipeline/migrate/db.py reads when it loads the Postgres tracking
database. Every value here exists because events' taxonomy output and
payload shape differ from news's; db.py's own defaults are news's, so
this block is the whole of the difference.
EVENTS CANNOT BE UPDATED WITHOUT THIS DATABASE. event_article has no
sharepoint_id field, so the story table is the only link between a live
story and its export row. See Events-Pipeline/CLAUDE.md 5a.
_slug_suffix_comment: Every event slug ends in its SharePoint id. Decided 2026-08-12.
Events recur, so titles are not unique: 2,710 events share 2,373 titles.
26 are called 'EdTech Lounge Online' and all route to
regions/pk/entities/qtl/events; 19 are 'Virtual Open Day' under ismc.
Measured over all 2,710: a plain title slug gives 201 colliding paths
across 542 events. upload.py checks with_slug before creating, so the
second event finds the first and PUTs over it -- 542 would collapse
into 201 and 341 events would vanish with no error, and the
sharepoint_id -> sb_story_id mapping the update plans depend on would
The start date was measured too and is NOT enough: 98 events share a
title AND a day. Only the id is guaranteed unique (2,710 distinct).
Chosen over suffixing only the clashes because a slug must not depend
on what other events exist -- otherwise an edited title in a future
export silently changes a different event's public URL.
News and blogs do not set this and keep clean title slugs; their
headlines are near-unique, which events' are not.
_columns_comment: department and surface_global are null because events has neither: there
is no department signal in the export, and AdditionalEntity is empty on
all 2,710 so nothing is shared across entities.
target_full_slug is null because routing.csv records the destination
FOLDER, not a full story path. upload.py derives the slug from the title,
which is what news does too whenever target_slug is empty.
_assets_comment: News keeps every file in media[]. Events' media[] holds ONLY the 163
rich-text documents, on 120 of 2,710 stories -- the heroes are bare
filenames on content.banner and content.attachment, which is why those
media[] rather than richtext_media[], though they hold the same 163
files: richtext_media names them local_filename/local_src, and db.py
reads filename/src. Pointed at richtext_media the load skips all 163
Left at news's default this loads 163 rows, misses all 2,669 banners, and
still exits 0: the uploader then finds nothing to send and every event
publishes with an empty banner_image. It fails quietly, so check the
asset count after a load rather than the exit code.

_skip_steps_comment: Steps events does not need, and one it must not run.
Metadata.csv as a MEDIA MANIFEST with role and filename columns, which is what
news's was. Events' Metadata.csv is the CONTENT -- the images are named in the
imageurl and attachment_files columns instead -- so these three have nothing to
work out. Blogs skips the first two for the same reason.
extract-viewer-filters MUST be skipped. It writes to
storyblok-viewer/src/constants/, which is NOT per type -- it is news's review
viewer. Running it with --type events would overwrite news's tag, author,
publisher and contentWriter lists with events data. Events has no author or
publisher column at all, so it would write empty files over a finished corpus.
NOT skipped: the four richtext-media steps. The bodies contain zero , but
they do carry 363 document links -- 339 PDFs, 15 docx, 3 doc, 6 jpg -- which
live on aku.edu and die with the site. Those steps are what fetches them.
_content_fields_comment: The events story payload. Deliberately NOT a copy of news's 44 keys: the
events list has 36 columns, 4 dead on all 2,710, and none of news's alternate-
language, approver, pull-quote or globally-active fields exist at all.
Declaring only what the export actually has means a null in a built payload is
a real absence rather than a column nobody mapped. That is the blogs rule, and
it is why there is no `pull_quote` key here -- events has no such column, so
carrying an always-null field would only invite someone to look for the data.
Nine keys carry columns event_article has NO FIELD for -- contact, subtitle,
social_media, ongoing. They are kept in the payload on purpose: when the dev
adds a field, the data is already there and only build_payload changes. Losing
it here would mean re-running stage 1 over 2,710 events to get it back.
